title: Does iGRPO Need a Good Draft? Best-vs-Worst Self-Conditioning Ablation for RLVR Math

contributions.purpose: Isolate whether iGRPO's benefit comes from conditioning on high-quality drafts or from the two-stage structure itself.
contributions.mechanism: A controlled ablation comparing three matched-compute conditions on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B: GRPO baseline, iGRPO with best-of-N draft selection, and iGRPO with worst-of-formatted draft selection.
contributions.evaluation: All conditions use identical compute (8 rollouts/prompt, 131 training steps, 2 seeds) across six math benchmarks.
contributions.source_quote: (1) we design a clean ablation study that isolates the role of draft quality in iGRPO by comparing best-of-N vs worst-of-formatted draft selection under matched compute

contributions.purpose: Show that draft quality is not necessary for iGRPO's performance benefit.
contributions.mechanism: Worst-of-formatted draft selection (intentionally low-quality but well-formatted drafts) is compared against best-of-N selection.
contributions.evaluation: iGRPO-worst achieves 64.37% vs best-of-N's 61.94% macro-average accuracy (+2.43pp) with a recovery ratio of 1.34 (95% CI [1.21, 1.47]) on MATH500.
contributions.source_quote: (2) we demonstrate that draft quality is not necessary for iGRPO's benefit, with worst-of-formatted selection achieving a recovery ratio of 1.34 over best-of-N

contributions.purpose: Explain why worst-of-formatted draft selection outperforms best-of-N.
contributions.mechanism: Mechanistic analysis of gradient-active training groups (groups with nonzero reward standard deviation) under each condition.
contributions.evaluation: Worst-of-formatted selection increases gradient-active training groups by 50%, offered as a potential explanation for its superior performance.
contributions.source_quote: (3) we provide mechanistic analysis showing that worst-of-formatted selection increases gradient-active training groups by 50%, offering a potential explanation for its superior performance

notes: Contributions stated as an inline 'Our contributions are threefold' paragraph on page 2, not a bullet list. Deflationary/negative-style result: draft quality is claimed unnecessary for iGRPO, suggesting the method can be simplified. Pages 1-2 contain intro and method only; no related-work section seen, and no sentence positions this paper itself as extending/adapting prior work (intro only describes how prior iGRPO extends GRPO).
